notes: FROZEN (daemon=incapable, route=frozen) — no phases, per the SKILL frozen rule. The CORRECT spec, asserted here and never weakened to the daemon limit: user-esc-interrupt is ready → working → ready. A >2s prompt drives ready → working; the user interrupts mid-turn; state MUST settle back to ready (must not stick in working); a follow-up prompt drives a clean second ready → working → ready arc on the same session. Hermes CANNOT be observed for this today. It persists no transcript file — the daemon reads one shared SQLite store ($HERMES_HOME/state.db, ProcessOwnedStore) whose only turn boundary is messages.finish_reason='stop', and an interrupted turn never produces one: the InterruptedError path (conversation_loop.py:3070-3101) appends either a partial assistant row with finish_reason NULL or nothing at all, close_interrupted_tool_sequence's 'Operation interrupted.' row also carries no finish_reason, and the 'close the turn with final_response' block is explicitly gated on `not interrupted`. The in-memory turn_exit_reason ('interrupted_by_user' / 'interrupted_during_api_call') is never persisted and the store has no turns table, so Watcher.turnIsDone stays false, the parser emits assistant_message rather than turn_done, and classifier rule user_interrupt (which needs LastWasUserInterrupt, produced only by claudecode) can never fire — the session sticks in working until the NEXT turn completes or ended_at is set at CLI exit. Unfreeze = (daemon) a hook tier on Hermes' on_session_end hook, which fires at the end of EVERY turn carrying interrupted:bool + completed:bool (turn_finalizer.py:668-684, shell_hooks.py:87-93), + (driver) an interrupt step in driver-interactive.sh that sends C-c once (Escape is NOT bound to interrupt in Hermes; Ctrl+C at cli.py:14326 is, and a second press within 2s force-exits). Then re-assess to yes/full/ready, add the ready→working→ready phases, and record. Observations: the store does carry per-session input/output tokens on the sessions row, so tokens_nonzero holds; model and cost stay unpinned because the recorded model depends on which config.yaml the run's HERMES_HOME carries.
